'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict (2015–present)|Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict]]
***The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] say that they have struck [[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Abha International Airport]] and [[King Abdulaziz International Airport]] in [[Jeddah]] with [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]]. A Houthi spokesman said on [[Twitter]] that the attacks halted operations in the airports for two hours. The Saudi-led coalition says that it intercepted drones heading towards the kingdom but did not confirm the attacks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-security-yemen/yemens-houthis-say-they-have-struck-saudis-jeddah-abha-airports-with-drones-idUSKBN2AF0X1?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War]]
***[[Israeli Air Force|Israeli]] [[airstrike]]s on [[Iran]]ian weapons and missile depots near [[Damascus]], [[Syria]], kill six foreign nationals, according to the [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]]. The [[headquarters]] of the [[Syrian Army]]'s [[4th Armoured Division (Syria)|4th Armoured Division]] is also hit. [https://www.jewishpress.com/news/middle-east/syria/update-israeli-airstrikes-in-syria-kill-6-destroy-iranian-weapons/2021/02/15/ (''Jewish Press'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Operation Barkhane]] 
***[[President of Chad|Chadian President]] [[Idriss Déby]] announces that [[Government of Chad|his government]] will deploy 1,200 [[Military of Chad|troops]] to the [[tripoint]] of the [[Burkina Faso–Mali border|Burkina Faso–Mali]] and [[Burkina Faso–Niger border|Burkina Faso–Niger borders]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210215-chad-s-deby-says-deploying-soldiers-to-tackle-jihadists-in-sahel (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]], aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[Myanmar]]'s [[State Administration Council|military junta]] deploys [[Tatmadaw]] troops and cuts [[Internet]] services in many parts of the country hours after security forces fired [[Live ammo|live rounds]] to disperse a [[demonstration (military)|demonstration]] in the northern state of [[Kachin State|Kachin]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/myanmar-junta-cuts-internet-as-troops-fire-to-break-up-protest (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[2021 Erbil missile attacks]]
**Multiple rockets strike near [[Erbil International Airport]] in [[Kurdistan Region]], [[Iraq]], killing a foreign civilian contractor and wounding nine others, including a [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. service]] member. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/15/north-iraq-airbase-hosting-us-troops-targeted-by-several-rockets (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Bishop [[David Zubik]] of the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh Diocese]] announces that four Catholic elementary schools are merging to form two schools for the school year beginning in fall 2021. The decision comes after more than a year's deliberation and hours of study. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/pittsburgh-diocese-announces-mergers-for-four-catholic-schools-38981 (Catholic News Agency)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]], [[Economy of Denmark]]
***[[Denmark]]'s [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] contracts 3.7% in 2020, which is the first annual economic contraction since 2009 due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]. [https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/penge/dansk-oekonomi-bloeder-men-saerligt-en-ting-redder-os-paa-maalstregen (DR)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[economy of Japan]]
***[[Japan]]'s [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] contracts 4.8% in 2020, which is the first annual economic contraction since 2009 due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-56066065 (BBC News)]
*The [[World Trade Organization]] formally appoints former [[Finance Minister of Nigeria]] [[Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala]] as its first [[Africa]]n and first female [[Director-General of the World Trade Organization|Director-General]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-15/wto-formally-appoints-okonjo-iweala-as-its-first-female-leader (Bloomberg)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Congo River disaster]]
**A passenger [[barge]] crashes and capsizes on the [[Congo River]] in [[Mai-Ndombe Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing at least 60 people, while 240 others are reported missing. At least 300 people have been rescued from the river. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-disaster/at-least-60-killed-after-passenger-barge-crashes-on-congo-river-idUSKBN2AF1SD?il=0 (Reuters)]
*At least 37 people are killed by a bus falling off a bridge into a canal in [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/16/dozens-dead-after-bus-plunges-into-canal-in-central-india (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] begins the second phase of its vaccination programme for people over the age of 60 against COVID-19 in more than 300 municipalities. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/15/mexico-begins-vaccinating-elderly-against-covid-19 (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Connecticut]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from [[Fairfield County, Connecticut|Fairfield County]] with no known international travel history, which was notified by health officials in [[New York (state)|New York]]. [https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/coronavirus/south-african-covid-19-variant-detected-in-connecticut-resident/2423116/ (WVIT-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
*****[[Mississippi]] reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.djournal.com/news/first-case-of-covid-19-variant-strain-confirmed-in-mississippi/article_84cefcb3-7111-5ab2-a997-bae420a12eb3.html (''Daily Journal'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****[[Australia]] suspends its quarantine-free travel bubble arrangement with [[New Zealand]] after the discovery of three new community cases in [[Auckland]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-56063335 (BBC News)]
****Australia receives 142,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-15/pfizer-coronavirus-vaccine-doses-arrive-australia-rollout/13155726 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] receives 60,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://i.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/300230422/covid19-first-batch-of-pfizer-coronavirus-vaccine-arrives-in-new-zealand (Stuff.co.nz)]
****[[Auckland]] enters level three restrictions for the next three days in response to an ongoing [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] outbreak, closing all non-essential businesses and suspending all in-person education. The rest of the country will enter level 2 restrictions, which will limit public gatherings. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/14/new-zealand-covid-outbreak-race-to-trace-three-local-cases-in-auckland (''The Guardian'')]
****[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] confirms that three members of a family in Auckland who tested positive for COVID-19 are infected with the [[Lineage B.1.1.7|UK variant]] and that this is not connected to any managed isolation or [[quarantine]] facilities. [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/auckland-family-contracted-covid-19-have-uk-variant-not-connected-miq-ardern (TVNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Cambodia]] reports their first three cases of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]] in 28-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman from [[India]] and a 23-year-old woman who travelled from [[China]]. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50814311/first-cases-of-new-c-19-variant-found-in-cambodia/ (''Khmer Times'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Iraq]] announces that they will re-impose a partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] from February 18 until March 8 after reporting their first cases of the UK variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1809811/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] surpasses 7,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/02/15/21/japans-covid-19-death-count-tops-7000 (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The [[Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency]] scales back Q1 vaccination targets to 750,000 people due to delayed shipments from [[COVAX]] and the decision not to use the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]] vaccine on people aged 65 or older until more efficacy data becomes available. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southkorea/s-korea-cuts-q1-covid-19-vaccination-plan-restricts-use-of-astrazeneca-shot-idUSKBN2AF07K?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]]ese [[Government of Vietnam|authorities]] order two million people in [[Hải Dương]] province to [[Stay-at-home order|stay at home]] for 15 days beginning tomorrow due to a growing COVID-19 outbreak in the province. Gatherings with more than two people are banned, and when leaving their homes, residents must stay {{convert|2|m|ft}} from others. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-vietnam-stay-home-orders-hai-duong-hotspot-14202214 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****The [[United Kingdom]] begins a mandatory hotel quarantine for all [[British people|British]] and [[Irish people|Irish]] citizens and all permanent residents arriving in [[England]] from 33 "high risk" countries, requiring them to stay for 10 days at government-designated accommodations. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-02-15/first-guests-to-check-into-quarantine-hotels-for-10-day-stay (ITV)] [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/uk/british-and-irish-arriving-in-england-must-now-quarantine-in-hotels-1.4485179 (''The Irish Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]] begins a mandatory hotel [[quarantine]] for all international arrivals, requiring them to self-isolate for 10 days in one of six government-designated hotels. [https://news.stv.tv/scotland/hotel-quarantine-begins-for-international-arrivals-to-scotland (STV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia]]
****[[Colombia]] receives their first shipment of 50,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-02-colombia-shipment-coronavirus-vaccines.html (MedicalXpress)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] receives their first shipment of 200,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3121787/chinese-vaccines-reach-zimbabwe-it-receives-its-first (''South China Morning Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[World Health Organization]] announces the approval of the [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]–[[AstraZeneca]] [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2021/02/15/astrazeneca-oxford-covid-19-vaccine-gets-emergency-approval-from-who/?sh=350b511d3953 (''Forbes'')]
*An [[Ebola]] [[vaccination]] campaign begins in the city of [[Butembo]], in the eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. Health workers are the first to be vaccinated. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-ebola-congo/ebola-vaccination-campaign-begins-in-democratic-republic-of-congo-idUSKBN2AF16Y (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Turkey–United States relations]], [[Operation Claw-Eagle 2]]
**[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] accuses the [[United States]] of supporting "the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party|PKK]] [[terrorism in Turkey|terrorists]]", following the killing of 13 Turkish [[hostage]]s held captive in [[Kurdistan Region]]. Turkey also summons the U.S. [[ambassador]] [[David M. Satterfield]] in response to the killings. [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/war-on-terror/erdogan-slams-us-for-siding-with-pkk-terrorists (''Daily Sabah'')]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[Iran]] says that it has informed the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] that it will no longer allow snap inspections of its nuclear facilities as of February 21. The snap inspections were a condition of the 2015 [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Iranian nuclear deal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-usa-iaea/iran-says-it-has-told-iaea-of-plan-to-end-snap-inspections-idUSKBN2AF1K4 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]], [[January 6 commission]]
**[[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] announces that [[United States Congress|Congress]] will establish a [[9/11 Commission|9/11-style]] commission to investigate the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-capitol-siege-acquittals-impeachments-trump-impeachment-7ebcbaedd6985537dec0c3918cbf06d9 (AP)]
*Turkish authorities announce the detention of 718 people they accuse of having links to [[Kurds|Kurdish]] militant groups. Among those arrested include pro-Kurdish [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]] officials. The [[mass arrest]]s are seen as a direct response to the murder of 13 Turkish hostages in Iraq. The [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] blamed Turkish [[airstrike]]s on their bases for the deaths of the hostages. [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20210215-turkey-arrests-hundreds-over-alleged-kurdish-militant-links-in-iraq-executions (France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Peru]]
**[[President of Peru|President]] [[Francisco Sagasti]] appoints [[Allan Wagner Tizón]] as new [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Peru)|foreign minister]], a day after [[Elizabeth Astete]] resigned over secretly receiving a vaccination against [[COVID-19]]. [https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-peru-new-foreign-affairs-minister-sworn-in-833806.aspx (Andina)]

**[[Michael McDowell (racing driver)|Michael McDowell]] wins the [[2021 Daytona 500|63rd running]] of the [[Daytona 500]]. It is McDowell's first career victory in the Cup Series. [https://www.nascar.com/news-media/2021/02/15/results-cup-series-2021-daytona-500-race-recap/ (NASCAR.com)]
